To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the family B ϕ 29 DNA polymerase preferentially insert dC opposite 6-oxo-2′-dG, its 3’-5’ exonuclease activity act indistinctly against both dA or C primer terminus and the extension of the 6-oxodG:dG base pair is favoured over the 6-0xodG:dA one.
the highly conserved Tyr390 of family B DNA Pol contributes to dictate nucleotidyl transfer preferences during translesional synthesis of 8oxo-7-8-dihydro-dG.

the highly conserved Tyrr residue of family B polymerases contributes to the ability of ϕ29 DNA replicase to discriminate between the two base pairs of the 8-oxoguanine lesion, and that the presence of the aromatic ring is necessary for the extension of the 7,8-dioxo-2′-dG/adenine base pair, whereas the presence of the hydroxil group is necessary to favour the extension of the correct base pair.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of a highly conserved residue in translesion synthesis, and provides a new insight on the mechanism of translesional synthesis by ϕ29 DNA Polymerase, a model replicase from the B family.
the identification and characterisation of the molecular determinants of family B replicases that are relevant to dictate the translesion synthesis of 8oxoG-containing DNA templates.
the identification of a highly conserved residue of family B replicases that contributes to dictate trans-lesion synthesis past a mutagenic lesion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this residue is not a key determinant for the discrimination against 8oxodA, but it contributes to the favoured extension of the correct 8oxodC base pair, and to the lack of extension of the incorrect 8oxodAdA pair.
ϕ29 DNA Pol B has a strong preference for dC insertion opposite 8-oxoguanine, and that this preference is dictated by the presence of a tyrosine residue in motif B.
ϕ29 DNA Pol B has evolved to prefer dC insertion opposite 8-oxodG, and that this preference is dictated by Tyr390.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 8oxoG/dA pair is a preferred substrate for translesion synthesis by family B polymerases, which would be consistent with a potential role of these enzymes in the repair of 8oxo-dG lesions.

the translesion synthesis ability of family A DNA polymerases on 8oxogG is mainly dictated by its exonuclease activity, whereas family B DNA polymerase ability to discriminate between dA and dC is mainly dictated by the presence of an aromatic residue in its motif B.
ϕ29 DNA Polymerase discriminates against the 8oxo-7-8-dihydroguanine (8oxodGu) base pair by inserting dCMP, and that this is due to the presence of the conserved Tyr390 residue.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of this highly conserved residue in the family B polymerases may contribute to the fidelity of translesion synthesis, which is a critical process in the prevention of the accumulation of mutations.

, although the Y390 residue does not participate in the direct recognition of 8oxo-7-8-dihydroguanine, it is required for the correct discrimination against dA and the favoured extension of the correct dC pair.
family B DNA polymerase can discriminate between dA and dC insertion opposite 8-oxodG, but the efficiency of the extension step depends on the nature of the base pair formed.
